source.author: cic
source.text: Democritus luminibus amissis alba scilicet discernere et atra non poterat, at vero bona mala, aequa iniqua, honesta turpia, utilia inutilia, magna parva poterat, et sine varietate colorum licebat vivere beate, sine notione rerum non licebat.
source.text_original: Democritus luminibus amissis alba scilicet discernere et atra non poterat, at vero bona mala, aequa iniqua, honesta turpia, utilia inutilia, magna parva poterat, et sine varietate colorum licebat vivere beate, sine notione rerum non licebat.
source.text_english: Democritus, when his eyesight had been lost, could of course no longer distinguish white from black, but he could distinguish good from bad, what is fair from unfair, what is honorable from shameful, what is useful from useless, what is great from small; and without an awareness of colors it was possible to live happily, but without an understanding of things it was not possible.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: denique quosdam etiam mundi philosophos legimus, ut totam cogitationem ad mentis cogerent puritatem, sibi oculos eruisse.
reuse.text_original: denique quosdam etiam mundi philosophos legimus, ut totam cogitationem ad mentis cogerent puritatem, sibi oculos eruisse.
reuse.text_english: Finally, we have even read of certain philosophers of the world who, in order to compel all their thought to the purity of the mind, gouged out their own eyes.
